[ASSISTANT_SAID] To ensure a baby is getting enough milk while breastfeeding, monitor baby's weight, check baby's diapers, observe feeding patterns, check baby's behavior, consult with a lactation consultant, practice proper latching techniques, and increase nursing sessions.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] A baby should gain around 5-7 ounces per week.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] A baby who is getting enough milk should have around six to eight wet diapers a day and six to eight dirty diapers a week.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] A baby who is getting enough milk will feed every 2-3 hours and appear content after a feeding.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Pumping breast milk between feedings can help increase milk supply by stimulating production.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Pumping should be done in addition to breastfeeding, not as a replacement.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Common reasons for low milk supply include infrequent breastfeeding or pumping, poor latch, stress and fatigue, health problems, and medications.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Preventing low milk supply is not always possible, but mothers can promote milk production by breastfeeding or pumping frequently, ensuring a proper latch, and taking care of themselves.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Staying hydrated is important, but drinking more water alone may not increase milk supply.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Dehydration can affect milk production, so breastfeeding mothers should drink enough fluids to stay hydrated.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Foods with high water content, such as fruits and vegetables, can also contribute to hydration.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] A mother's diet can impact her milk supply; a balanced diet is important.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] There is no specific food that must be avoided, but some mothers may notice certain foods affect their baby's feeding patterns.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Common triggers include dairy, soy, wheat, nuts, and caffeine.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Breastfeeding mothers should incorporate plenty of fruits, vegetables, whole grains, protein sources, and healthy fats into their diet.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Supplements that may help increase milk supply include fenugreek, blessed thistle, milk thistle, brewer's yeast, and fennel.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] It's important to consult with a healthcare provider before taking any supplements.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] A mother's stress level can affect the taste and quality of her breast milk due to increased cortisol levels.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Regular self-care practices can help
